definition: A problem-solving approach is a way of structuring routine clinical conversations so patients’ own assessments and expressed needs are used to work collaboratively on ways forward. In this context, it supports patient involvement and a more patient-centred style of care.

reasons: The definition’s claims about a general “problem-solving approach” (as a way to structure routine clinical conversations) are not explicitly defined in the packet; the packet only describes DIALOG+ as incorporating a “problem-solving approach” within routine encounters.

The definition asserts that it uses “patients’ own assessments and expressed needs” to work collaboratively on “ways forward”; the packet mentions self-assessment and expressed needs in relation to patient involvement, but it does not state this as the general defining function of a “problem-solving approach.”
The definition is placed in the field “diagnosis,” but the packet provides context about outpatient psychosis care and patient involvement, not diagnostic criteria or a diagnostic sense of the term.

The definition characterizes the approach as supporting patient involvement and a “more patient-centred style of care”; while the packet supports patient involvement and patient-centred care in the context of DIALOG+, it does not present these as defining features of the term itself outside that intervention.
The packet only mentions a problem-solving approach as one component of the DIALOG+ intervention; it does not define the term as a general counselling/clinical-conversation method.

“Routine clinical conversations,” “patients’ own assessments,” and “expressed needs” are only partially supported by the packet, which refers to routine clinical encounters, self-assessment, and treatment focusing on expressed needs, but not the full explanatory wording in the definition.
The claim that this approach is used to “work collaboratively on ways forward” goes beyond the packet’s wording and is not directly supported as a definition of the term.
